Subject: CloudCart reseller addendum & pass-through evidence — initial draft

Hi Sofia,

Attaching our draft of the reseller/marketplace addendum (CloudCart-Addendum_v1.docx). Legal on our side asked for a clearer picture of what evidence Redwood expects when we pass fees through to the end customer — specifically:

- What invoice mapping fields do you need (invoice id, customer id, usage window)?
- Minimum retention period for logs for audit requests.
- Format you prefer for bulk evidence (CSV vs signed PDF bundles).

We also want to understand the operational sequence you expect for pass-through credits vs refunds (who issues the credit, timeline, rollback if disputed). Our procurement lead (Asha Patel) may join follow-ups.

Can you confirm whether your team needs escrow/account-level invoice traces or if aggregated reporting will suffice for initial onboarding?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call.

Jules Mercer
Head of Partnerships | CloudCart
[Attachment: CloudCart-Addendum_v1.docx (DOCX, 210KB)]

Subject: Re: CloudCart reseller addendum & pass-through evidence — initial draft

Hi Jules — thanks for sending this over and for the clear list of questions. I looped in Marissa (partner ops), Ben (revenue ops / billing), and Irene (legal) so we can align on both the contractual language and the operational handoff.

High-level from our side:
- Evidence: for the audit / pass-through proofs we typically require invoice-level mappings (invoice id, partner invoice ref, end-customer id/email, charge timestamp, usage window). CSV is preferred for bulk uploads; PDFs are OK for one-off audit artifacts.
- Retention: 18 months is our standard for pass-through traceability; we can discuss a shorter window for low-dollar partners but need >12 months for reconciliation.
- Sequence: our usual flow is: partner submits invoice -> Redwood validates mapping -> if discrepancy, partner has 14 days to provide additional proof -> if unresolved, we provision a provisional credit then reconcile on next billing cycle. Need to reflect that in the addendum.

Irene, Ben — attached is CloudCart’s draft. Can you review the pass-through and escrow clauses and propose concrete language we can send back? Marissa, can you sync with Jules offline for the operational cadence (SLA on evidence requests, API spec for CSV columns)?

I'll share our evidence checklist to help them format deliverables.

Best,
Sofia
Director, Partner Programs | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_evidence_checklist.pdf (PDF, 85KB)]

Quick internal notes / suggested bullets for redlines (I ran this by ops):

- Audit window: propose 12 months minimum, 18 months preferred (we can make 12 months baseline + 6-month extension for enterprise).
- Data artifacts: require CSV with columns: invoice_id, partner_invoice_id, end_customer_id, sku, usage_quantity, usage_start, usage_end, tax_amount, gross_amount, net_amount, currency, timestamp.
- Escrow/audit clause: move to separate appendix that defines "acceptable evidence" and the audit request process (30-day notice, scope-limited to disputed invoices).
- Credits / sequencing: add explicit sequence: (1) partner submits evidence; (2) Redwood issues provisional credit within 7 business days if mapping validates; (3) final reconciliation on next billing cycle; (4) disputed items revert if partner-provided evidence fails verification within 30 days.
- Liability carveout: limit partner liability to fees collected in the affected invoice(s) unless fraud is suspected.

I also recommend we require a machine-readable manifest (CSV) and provide a secure SFTP or presigned S3 upload path for large batches. Marissa, can you confirm ops SLA and preferred ingest endpoints so we can put language in the addendum?

-Ben

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudCart reseller addendum & pass-through evidence — suggested legal redlines

Thanks — I reviewed CloudCart-Addendum_v1 and drafted focused redlines. Key legal points to propose back:

1) Mutual audit protocol: we add a one-page appendix that lists acceptable PoE (proofs of entitlement) artifacts: invoice CSV (schema above), signed purchase orders, customer subscription IDs, and S3 access logs for the specific invoice window. Audit requests limited to a 12-month lookback by default; 18 months only if mutually agreed.

2) Indemnity / liability: narrow the reseller indemnity to third-party claims arising from reseller-modified pricing or misrepresentation. For simple pass-through misallocations, cap liability at amounts actually passed through in the relevant invoices (no punitive damages).

3) Escrow / holdback language: add a clause for provisional credits and a 30-day dispute remediation period; if partner fails to provide required artifacts within 30 days, Redwood may offset credits against future payouts.

4) Data security & transfer: require that any CSVs or logs are transferred via encrypted channels (S3 presigned URL or SFTP) and that CloudCart confirms retention policies and deletion schedules.

5) Rollback & reconciliation: include an explicit reconciliation cadence (monthly) and a process for issuing reversals along with a requirement that partner provide a remediation plan for recurring discrepancies.

I attached a PDF with redline snippets (sofia_marketplace_redlines_v2.pdf). Once we have their procurement contact, I recommend a 30-minute legal+ops call to go over the appendix and the ingest format.

Irene Choi
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sofia_marketplace_redlines_v2.pdf (PDF, 72KB)]
